# Code Review — 2026-07-19

- [ ] **[Security] Replace the body-suffix conflict guard in meeting frontmatter writes with a content-hash check**
  - **Status quo:** `writeMeetingFrontmatter` detects concurrent modification only via `strings.HasSuffix(rawStr, doc.Body)` (`internal/service/meeting_people.go:102`). A concurrent frontmatter-only change (participant confirm from the app vs. `meeting`/MCP review save, or a publish updating the `symmeet_published_facts` ledger via `vault.SetFrontmatterValue`, `internal/service/meeting_publish.go:133`) leaves the body unchanged, so the guard passes and the stale frontmatter silently overwrites the newer one — losing confirmations or the published-facts ledger, which re-opens the duplicate-Memory-writes bug that #190 fixed. `doc.SHA256` is already computed at parse time (`internal/vault/vault.go:149`).
  - **Proposed solution:** Hash the re-read file content and compare it against `doc.SHA256` instead of the body-suffix check; return the existing "changed on disk since it was read; re-run" error on mismatch. Add a regression test where a frontmatter-only change lands between read and write (including a publish-ledger update) and assert the write is refused.
  - **Effort/Impact:** Low effort / high impact

- [ ] **[Security] Stop sending unresolved `op://` secret references to the Anthropic API**
  - **Status quo:** When `llm_api_key` is an `op://` reference but `symvault` is not on `PATH`, `ResolveKey` falls through and returns the raw reference string as the API key (`internal/secrets/secrets.go:33`, `internal/secrets/secrets.go:48`); it is then sent verbatim as the `x-api-key` header to `api.anthropic.com` (`internal/ai/anthropic.go:50`), leaking the vault/item naming to a third party and surfacing only as an opaque HTTP 401. `Source` likewise reports `"symvault"` for any `op://` ref without checking availability (`internal/secrets/secrets.go:64`), so `doctor` output is misleading in exactly this broken state.
  - **Proposed solution:** Treat an `op://` reference without a usable `symvault` as a resolution failure: return empty (or an explicit error) so the existing "AI not configured" degradation path triggers with a message naming the missing tool, and make `Source` report the same failure state; cover both in `secrets_test.go`.
  - **Effort/Impact:** Low effort / medium impact

- [ ] **[UX/DX] Make the AI answer language configurable instead of hardcoded German**
  - **Status quo:** All `ask`/`transform` prompts force German output ("Antworte auf Deutsch", `internal/ai/ai.go:199`, `internal/ai/ai.go:208`) and every AI error/degradation message is German-only (`internal/ai/ai.go:86`, `internal/ai/ai.go:99`, `internal/ai/ai.go:152`), while the README, `--help`, and every other CLI surface are English. For a public Apache-2.0 tool this makes the flagship AI feature effectively single-locale.
  - **Proposed solution:** Add a `language` config field / `SYMDESK_LANG` env override (default: answer in the language of the query, error messages in English), thread it into `buildPrompt`/`buildTransformPrompt`, and move the user-facing degradation strings to the same mechanism.
  - **Effort/Impact:** Low effort / medium impact

- [ ] **[UX/DX] Surface Anthropic output truncation instead of silently cutting off at 4096 tokens**
  - **Status quo:** `streamAnthropic` hardcodes `max_tokens: 4096` (`internal/ai/anthropic.go:26`) and only consumes `content_block_delta` events (`internal/ai/anthropic.go:85`), ignoring `message_delta` with `stop_reason: "max_tokens"`. Long `transform --intent continue`/summarize outputs end mid-sentence with no indication anything was lost — locally, via the app AI dock, and through the server's streamed `/api/v1/command` path.
  - **Proposed solution:** Make the token limit configurable (config + env, sensible higher default), parse `message_delta` events, and on `stop_reason == "max_tokens"` emit an explicit trailing notice/error chunk so CLI, app, and NDJSON consumers can show "output truncated".
  - **Effort/Impact:** Low effort / medium impact

- [ ] **[Architecture] Inject config into `internal/ai` and deduplicate provider dispatch**
  - **Status quo:** `Ask`, `Transform`, and `promptOne` each re-load the global config and discard the error (`internal/ai/ai.go:77`, `internal/ai/ai.go:143`, `internal/ai/ai.go:238`), although `cmd/symdesk` already loads and validates it (`cmd/symdesk/main.go:48`) — a malformed config nil-panics in any call path that skips `initConfig`, and CLI-level overrides never reach the AI layer. The provider-dispatch and channel-drain logic is also copy-pasted three times (`internal/ai/ai.go:83`, `internal/ai/ai.go:149`, `internal/ai/ai.go:243`).
  - **Proposed solution:** Pass `*config.Config` (or a small provider settings struct) into `Ask`/`Transform`/`PromptOne`, collapse the three provider branches into one `providerStream(ctx, cfg, prompt, out)` helper, and delete the in-package `config.Load` calls; update the fake-based tests accordingly.
  - **Effort/Impact:** Low effort / medium impact

- [ ] **[Performance] Stop re-parsing every vault file per Memory entity in the graph endpoint**
  - **Status quo:** `Service.Graph` runs `vault.ParseFile(d.Path)` — full disk read, SHA-256, YAML parse — inside the per-entity loop (`internal/service/graph.go:72`, `internal/service/graph.go:75`), i.e. O(entities × documents) file I/O per `symdesk graph` call, because `ListFiles` rows lack the body that `matchesOther` needs (`internal/service/service.go:757`, `internal/sidecar/db.go:581`). Node/edge dedup is additionally an O(n²) linear scan (`internal/service/graph.go:98`, `internal/service/graph.go:124`), and each matched entity spawns a `GetNeighbors` subprocess (`internal/service/graph.go:93`). On the documented 10k-document vault with a few dozen entities this is hundreds of thousands of file parses per graph render (app GraphView and CLI).
  - **Proposed solution:** Resolve entity mentions via the existing FTS index (one `db.Search` per entity name/alias) or, at minimum, parse each document once before the entity loop and reuse it; replace the linear dedup scans with `map[string]struct{}` sets. Add a benchmark over the deterministic 10k fixture (`make benchmark-large` vault) covering graph generation with entities present.
  - **Effort/Impact:** Medium effort / high impact

## Conclusion

The first recommended quick win is the meeting-frontmatter conflict guard: `doc.SHA256` already exists, the fix is a few lines plus one regression test, and it closes a silent lost-update path that can re-introduce the duplicate-Memory-writes bug just fixed in #190.
